title: SQL Window Functions Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision of SQL window functions: OVER, PARTITION BY and ORDER BY, ranking functions, LAG/LEAD, running totals, frames and top-N per group.

chapters.title: Window Functions Mental Model
points: A window function computes a value per row over a set of related rows without collapsing them, unlike GROUP BY which returns one row per group
OVER() makes an aggregate or ranking function a window function; empty OVER() means the window is the whole result set
PARTITION BY splits rows into independent groups; the function restarts in each partition
ORDER BY inside OVER sets row order within a partition and, for aggregates, turns the default frame into a running one
Window functions run after WHERE, GROUP BY and HAVING but before the final ORDER BY and LIMIT, so they cannot appear in WHERE or HAVING

chapters.title: Ranking: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK
points: ROW_NUMBER() gives unique sequential numbers 1,2,3,4 even for ties; tie order is arbitrary unless you add a tiebreaker column
RANK() gives tied rows the same number and skips the next ones: 1,2,2,4
DENSE_RANK() gives tied rows the same number with no gaps: 1,2,2,3
Example: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) numbers employees within each department by pay
Gotcha: ranking without ORDER BY in OVER is meaningless or an error; always add a deterministic tiebreaker such as id for ROW_NUMBER

chapters.title: LAG and LEAD
points: LAG(col, n, default) reads the value n rows before the current row in window order; LEAD(col, n, default) reads n rows after
Defaults: n = 1 and default = NULL, so the first row of a partition returns NULL for LAG unless a default is given
Example: amount - LAG(amount) OVER (ORDER BY month) gives month-over-month change
Add PARTITION BY to stop LAG/LEAD reading across groups, e.g. per customer or per product
Gotcha: LAG/LEAD need ORDER BY to be meaningful, and NULL from the edge rows breaks arithmetic unless handled with COALESCE or the default argument

chapters.title: Running Totals and Frames
points: Frame clause: ROWS | RANGE | GROUPS BETWEEN start AND end, with bounds UNBOUNDED PRECEDING, n PRECEDING, CURRENT ROW, n FOLLOWING, UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
Running total: SUM(x) OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY d ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
Default frame with ORDER BY is RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING to CURRENT ROW; with no ORDER BY it is the whole partition
ROWS counts physical rows; RANGE includes all peers (rows with equal ORDER BY value), so tied dates give the same running total
Moving average: AVG(x) OVER (ORDER BY d ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) averages the last 7 rows
Gotcha: LAST_VALUE with the default frame returns the current row's peer, not the partition end; extend the frame to UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING

chapters.title: Top-N per Group and Common Mistakes
points: Top-N per group pattern: rank in a subquery or CTE, then filter the rank in the outer query: WHERE rn <= N
Window functions cannot be filtered in the same SELECT's WHERE; wrap in a CTE: WITH r AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY v DESC) rn FROM t) SELECT * FROM r WHERE rn <= 3
Use ROW_NUMBER for exactly N rows per group, RANK or DENSE_RANK to keep ties (may return more than N rows)
Latest row per group: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY updated_at DESC) = 1, then keep rn = 1
Gotcha: the ORDER BY inside OVER does not sort the output; add a final ORDER BY if you need ordered results

chapters.title: Window Functions Cheat Sheet
points: Syntax: func() OVER (PARTITION BY cols ORDER BY cols frame)
Ranking: ROW_NUMBER unique, RANK gaps on ties, DENSE_RANK no gaps
Offsets: LAG(col,n,default) looks back, LEAD(col,n,default) looks ahead
Running total: SUM(x) OVER (ORDER BY d ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
Top-N per group: ROW_NUMBER in a CTE, then WHERE rn <= N
Interview Point: ROW_NUMBER vs RANK vs DENSE_RANK on ties, and ROWS vs RANGE frame difference
